newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end stronger following 10-yr auction.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end stronger following 10-yr auction.

text.p: Canadian bonds rebounded to close stronger on Wednesday, helped by a well-received auction of Canadian 10-year bonds and a tame U.S. economic report, analysts said.

"I think you had two good things in your favor, one being a fairly decently bid 10-year Canadian auction, obviously a lot better bid than the U.S. 10-year auction. And you also had what was really a tame (U.S.) beige book," said Andrew Pyle, head of fixed income research with ABN-AMRO Bank Canada.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.32 to C$120.41 to yield 6.449 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 5/32 to yield 6.48 percent. The negative spread between the bonds widened to three basis points from two basis points at Tuesday's close.

The Canadian government's sale of C$2.3 billion of 6.0 percent bonds due June 1, 2008 produced an average yield of 6.079 percent and price of 99.392. The auction had a high low gap of 1.7 basis points and a tail of 0.8 percent reflecting firm buying interest, analysts said.
The auction results helped boost prices, along with the U.S. Fed Beige Book, which said the U.S. economy grew moderately in June and July with few signs of rising prices.

Analysts said one factor weighing on Canadian bond prices today was weakness in the currency. The dollar ended weaker around C$1.3875 (US$0.7207) on Wednesday from Tuesday's close at C$1.3800 (US$0.7246) amid selling on International Money Market.

Pyle said that if the currency weakened past C$1.39 (US$0.7194) on Thursday, it would increase speculation of a Bank of Canada rate hike, which would weigh on the short end of the Canadian yield curve.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.17 to C$109.60 to yield 5.942 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 5/32 to yield 6.21 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 27 basis points from 29 basis points at Tuesday's close.
